Why_Required: No catalogue provides a dedicated structured count of physical DIMM slots. Textual configuration may mention DIMM counts in some server records, but there is no consistent field across the catalogues.
There is no structured field identifying which DIMM slots are populated and with what module capacities.
CPU Memory_Configuration can say 'per socket', but a structured numeric memory-capacity-per-socket field is not present in the audited catalogues.
No uploaded catalogue contains a structured NUMA topology field describing memory nodes, CPU-to-memory-node mapping, or socket locality.
No field identifies local versus remote memory accessibility/placement for CPU sockets or devices.
Server and CPU bandwidth fields are marked derived or mixed derived/verified, and GPU bandwidth is hardware-specified; no measured sustained/application-level memory bandwidth field exists.
No uploaded catalogue contains a memory latency field for host DRAM/HBM or NUMA-local/remote access.
No structured field identifies workload, benchmark, concurrency/thread count, problem size, or measurement methodology for bandwidth values.
Hardware catalogues do not contain workload-level training memory demand. This is appropriately a future workload/rule-level input rather than a hardware catalogue field.
Hardware catalogues do not contain workload-level inference memory demand, including model/runtime/KV-cache demand. This is appropriately a future workload/rule-level input.
No catalogue records measured application memory consumption for training or inference workloads.
